channel.title: New Left Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from New Left Review (newleftreview.org)

item.title: Emilie Bickerton, Subterranean Godard, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: Emilie Bickerton on Michael Witt, Jean-Luc Godard’s Unmade and Abandoned Projects. A ‘negative’ history that sheds new light on the master filmmaker.

item.title: Nausicaa Renner, Party and Class, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: Nausicaa Renner on Paul Heideman, Rogue Elephant. Hollowed-out parties and capitalist sectoralization said to underlie the Trumpian capture of the GOP.

item.title: Tony Wood, A Bolivarian Republic of Letters?, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: Tony Wood on Julio Cortázar, Carlos Fuentes, Gabriel García Márquez and Mario Vargas Llosa, Las cartas del Boom. Correspondence between four titans of the midcentury Latin American novel.

item.title: Costas Lapavitsas, A Topography of the New Dollar Imperialism, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: Topography of the contemporary world economy as a system of subordination, structured by the primacy of Fed-backed dollar-liquidity and a world division of labour jointly configured by productive and financial capital, generating forms of peripheral financialization. Monetary dominance—ultimately underwritten by military force?

item.title: Rohana Kuddus, Prabowo’s Year One, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: A critical-analytical portrait of Southeast Asia’s answer to Trump, as the Indonesian President—formerly the Suharto dictatorship’s crown prince and chief butcher in East Timor—re-centralizes power in the archipelago, strengthening the Army’s place within the civil administration.

item.title: Xi Ruochen, In Search of Good Books, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: Where might Chinese-language readers hungry for critical histories and marginalized voices find such books? A history of Sinosphere publishing, charting the relationship between Hong Kong and the Mainland within a broader media ecology from the Revolution to the present.

item.title: Ervand Abrahamian, Iran Under Fire, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: One of modern Iran’s leading historians provides a critical anatomy of the power structures of the Islamic Republic, on the eve of war—and a scathing denunciation of the long-incubated American-Israeli assault on the country, calculated to bring about Syria-style disintegration and civil war.

item.title: Susan Watkins, Trump Abroad, NLR 157, January–February 2026
item.description: In which direction is America heading, amid the strategic cacophony of Trump’s second term—counter-revolution in the Caribbean, onslaught on Iran, somersaults on China? Analysis of the political logics at stake as the US ratchets up from covert to overt assassinations; from wars of attrition to wars of overthrow.
